title: Scarpelli's promise and the 1934 heat wave tour
summary: Scarpelli guarantees them the Club Plantation in the fall; on tour in Kansas, Walter Page collapses in 107 degree heat and they see the Dust Bowl.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Hayes, didn't Tony say before he took the choice of going with Jean Calloway, he said he would pay our transportation back to Cleveland --
Or he would give -- guarantee us a job in the Plantation Club, if we went with Jean Calloway.

That's right, that's what he did. He said if we wanted to go back to Cleveland, he would pay our way back to cleveland. He said if we want to stick around and take this tour and keep your band together, he would put us in the Club Plantation that FALL. That's what he did.

That's what he did. He kept his word, uh-huh. And we toured -- I'm trying to think -- oh, Manhattan, Kansas was a town we played, and Mr. Page -- who had been quite an athlete in college, this particular day was the hottest day in the history of Manhattan, Kansas and it was the hottest day I ever spent in my life, the temperature went up to about

107°. And Manhattan, Kansas, and Mr. Page was out there jogging and on some track and he fell out and we had to pour cold water over him to get him to -- to help him gain his conscious -- and he never did that anymore. But this was the hottest day that I had ever witnessed in my life. It was a hot summer.
See, they have no highway, but you had to roll the windows up --

Had to roll the windows up on the highway, it was cooler with the windows up in the car than it was with the -- with the windows down. And I remember driving through Oklahoma, that was when they had the dust bowl, and you could see dead cattle laying all out in the fields, you know? From the dust bowl and no water.
That was a -- another rough summer.
